Test wishlist to request from Dr. Brondfield (UCSF). BLOOD: Gastrin (fasting); Pepsinogen I+II + PGI/PGII ratio; Parietal cell + intrinsic factor antibodies; H. pylori IgG serology. STOOL: Pancreatic elastase-1; Fecal calprotectin; Lactoferrin; Steatocrit; Fecal fat; GI Effects + GI-MAP (whichever orderable). URINE: Urinary indican (Obermayer); Organic acids test (OAT); Urinary N-methylhistamine. NON-INVASIVE GI/IMAGING (no scope): Heidelberg pH capsule; Barium swallow / upper GI series; Gastric emptying scintigraphy (4hr); Barium esophagram; Esophageal manometry. REFLUX MEASUREMENT: 24hr pH catheter vs Bravo pH capsule (Bravo needs endoscopy+anesthesia). Capsule (pill) endoscopy for bleeding. Hiatal hernia test. Ulcer/hiatal hernia check normally needs endoscope. Also: ask for new GI Effects.

Acid reflux update: discovered severe acid reflux — believes it causes ~90% of panic attacks. Frequent sour taste, regurgitation. Ate raw salmon sushi. 9:41pm drank water — at first it bothered her, now settling and not bothering as much. Her read: acid reflux calming down rather than Xanax. AI note: agree reflux settling is the most likely driver of the water going down easier. Xanax (alprazolam) acts on GABA and can lower anxiety + visceral/gut-nerve hypersensitivity, so it CAN indirectly dull gut sensation via the gut-brain axis — but it doesn't act on the water or stomach acid itself, and its effect is slower/more diffuse. So reflux easing is the better explanation for the quick change; Xanax may be a minor background contributor at most.

💊 Xanax↔reflux (clues 2+3, AI-checked): more Xanax DURING reflux = worse first/better later (benzos relax the LES + slow acid clearance → worsen reflux); but more Xanax on an EMPTY stomach is NOT worse (no reflux to worsen) — confirms it. Plausible not proven (I dose at peak; alprazolam data thin). Do NOT change taper alone; bring to prescriber (supports my taper). 🍳 Reflux scores /10: Chicken 2, Eggs 3 (fried→5-6), Salmon 5 (fat+fish-histamine; leftover→6-7). Keep plain/baked/fresh/small, don't lie down after.
Xanax 0.12mg taken (~9:41pm) - suspected acid reflux panic attack

🔑 BIGGEST CLUE (eating helps OR hurts depending on my stomach state) — MY OWN WORDS: "When I'm in the middle of a stomach-induced panic attack — what I now think is an ACID-REFLUX panic — eating does NOT help. I feel instantly more nauseous, even after I've taken Xanax. But when I haven't eaten much and I'm faint and panicky, running on empty, then eating DOES help."

CLINICAL READ: These look like two opposite body states wearing the same "panic" mask. State A is a FULL, sour, refluxy stomach where my vagus nerve (gut-brain wire) is already firing — adding food stretches it more and pushes acid up, so nausea spikes; Xanax can't touch that because it calms my brain, not my stomach. State B is an EMPTY, hollow, faint state from going too long without food plus over-breathing — a small bland bite settles it. Same action (eating), opposite result, because the starting stomach state is opposite. SELF-TEST: sour/full/just-ate -> don't eat, treat as reflux (upright, ginger tea/water, in-4/out-6-8, wait). Hollow/faint/3-4h empty AND danger-screen clear -> eat 2-3 bites of a safe food, then STOP and recheck; if worse, it was reflux. Reflux/low-acid/SIBO still suspected not proven; don't change Xanax taper; screen faintness for non-hunger causes (orthostatic/PPPD/cardiac/UARS/Vibrio dehydration).
Burping a lot right now (9:30 PM)

⚠️⚠️ PEPPERMINT WORSENS ACID REFLUX ⚠️⚠️ — menthol relaxes the lower esophageal sphincter (LES), letting acid up. AVOID peppermint tea, candies, and plain peppermint oil/extract for nausea. USE INSTEAD: ginger (tea/chews/capsules), or vitamin B6, or Sea-Band acupressure. If peppermint is needed for gut, ONLY enteric-coated peppermint oil capsules (release in the intestine, bypass the esophagus).
